newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Oct inflation up to 0.73 pct.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Oct inflation up to 0.73 pct.

text.p: Consumer prices rose 0.73 percent in October, compared with a 0.5 percent rise in the same month last year and 0.32 percent in September, the government's National Institute of Information and Statistics (INEI) said Friday.
Accumulated inflation in the first nine months of 1996 was 9.99 percent, up from 8.3 percent in the same period last year, according to INEI figures published in the official daily El Peruano.
Consumer inflation fell to 10.2 percent in 1995 from 15.4 percent the previous year. The 1995 figure was the lowest in 23 years.

Although the government was originally hoping for single- digit inflation in 1996 and has agreed to a target of 9.5 percent to 11.5 percent with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the latest official for this year's inflation was 12 percent.
The government estimates next year's accumulated inflation will be nine percent and will drop to "the level of industrialized countries" by 2000.
